newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-85 pct of Queensland affected by native title.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-85 pct of Queensland affected by native title.

text.p: Queensland premier Rob Borbidge said on Thursday that he had received legal advice that up to 85 percent of the state could be subject to native title claims from Aboriginal groups.
"Advice to me from the Crown Solicitor this morning is that up to 85 percent of Queensland could be subject to native title," Borbidge told a news conference.
His statement follows an Australian High Court decision last month that native title could co-exist with Crown leases currently held by farmers and mining companies.

Borbidge said there was "a desperate need for certainty in land tenure across Queensland and Australia." He said he would be meeting with Prime Minister John Howard next week to have further discussions on the Native Title issue.

Borbidge also said he would be meeting with Northern Territory Chief Minister Shane Stone and West Australian Premier Richard Court this weekend aimed at presenting a united front on the states most affected by the Native Title decision.
"This is a critical issue that has to be resolved, not just for farmers and the mining industry but for Aboriginals as well," Borbidge said.
Borbidge said he preferred to see a legislative response to solve uncertainly created by the court decision.
However, he ruled out a state election on the issue.
"This is about finding a solution, not about finding an election," Borbidge said.
